subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What canonical custom emoji representation should OpenClaw expose for outgoing Telegram messages: a shared Markdown IR span, Telegram-owned entity payloads on message actions, or both with one conversion boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable API choice crosses shared message-tool schema, Telegram plugin ownership, Markdown IR, delivery chunking, and docs, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Choose a canonical entity/IR contract
options.body: Define the public representation first, then implement the Telegram wiring and tests against that single contract.

options.title: Keep raw HTML only
options.body: Treat preserved `<tg-emoji>` HTML as enough for now, leaving message-tool entity pass-through and caption/edit entity support unsolved.

options.title: Defer to a Telegram-specific action only
options.body: Add a narrow Telegram-only action field without expanding shared IR, trading faster delivery for a more channel-specific message-tool surface.

recommendation.title: Choose a canonical entity/IR contract
recommendation.body: Define the public representation first, then implement the Telegram wiring and tests against that single contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He already recorded the current maintainer-facing API-shape concern on this issue and is connected to recent shared message-tool history.
